performance.cable-capacity-basis: Cat6 24AWG cables, theoretical - FS 0U/1U Horizontal Cable Manager datasheet, specification table

physical.mounting-hardware: M6*15mm Screw x4 and M6 Nut x4

configs.description: The lacer panel as FS ships #72911, five rings fitted.
configs.name: base

gaps.note: no document says how far the tray stands from the face of the device it is mounted over, or what it may be mounted over besides FS's own enclosures.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned installation figure, or a ruler on the part
no bays and no grouped ports to correlate against, so there is nothing to wire yet - group the ports first - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays
a port the DCIM export types as an interface - a placement in a group whose role is a port role, with media and speed it maps - unlocks interfaces on the NetBox / Nautobot device type

attrs.note: datasheet - the weight, the mounting hardware, "Indoor" and the ring material are in the 0U/1U datasheet's table. "Steel, Powder-coated Black" and "RoHS" are the specification table of FS's product page for #72911, which words the panel material and the standard more fully than the datasheet's "Steel" and its REACH, CE and UKCA badges; so is the 1.5 mm gauge. The page is not a held document.

cable-capacity.note: datasheet - "Cable Capacity (Theoretical Value) 30pcs (Cat6 24AWG)" in the 0U/1U datasheet's table, for the whole manager. Stated once, here, and not divided among the rings (docs/cable-managers-design.md, decision 9).

chassis.note: drawing - the same three-view: 483 overall and 44 high on the front view, 110 deep on the plan. The datasheet's table gives 44 x 482.6 x 109 mm (1.73 x 19.00 x 4.29 in); the depth taken is the drawing's 110, which measures 109.7, and the table's 109 is 4.29 in. `ru: 1` is the rack unit the ears span, from the 44 and the table's "Number of Rack Units: 0U" read as what it occupies. The 483 INCLUDES THE EARS, as it must on a part that is a bracket: the tray's body is 448.4 between them.

color.note: estimated - "Steel, Powder-coated Black" and "Color: Black". Every image FS publishes of the part is a render.

ears.note: drawing - THE EARS ARE DRAWN, where every other device in the library leaves them off. They are not something added to this part: they are the same sheet as the tray, and the part is nothing but them and what hangs off them.

front.note: drawing - an elevation: the ears, the edge of the tray and the five rings end-on, projected from the plan and ring-profile views. None of it lies in the front plane, and none of it is built in 3D from this view.

method.note: FIGURES FIRST, FROM THE VENDOR'S OWN DIMENSIONED DRAWING. The three-view drawing in FS's 0U/1U Horizontal Cable Manager Datasheet (updated 2025-05-11) is a 1142 x 767 px raster, the size it is embedded at, so nothing is gained by rendering the page. Its scale is 1.331 px/mm from the 483 dimension line (643 px), and the 465 (619 px), 110 (146 px), 44 (58 px) and 31.5 (42 px) lines all agree with it to a pixel, on both axes: the drawing is orthographic and carries geometry, to 0.75 mm.

mount.note: drawing - FS's Horizontal Cable Managers Quick Start Guide V2.0 draws the part's ear laid over the ear of an FHD fibre enclosure, one fastener each side, with the tray hanging in front of the enclosure's face. Not dimensioned, and the only host drawn is that enclosure. The datasheet says it mounts "on either the front or rear".

rear.note: drawing - the front view, seen here from behind: an ear at each end, 17.3 wide and 44 high, the tray's edge and the five rings end-on between them, with fixing holes 9 mm in from the end (the 465 between centres) and 31.5 apart. A third hole between them is in the quick start guide's figure and FS's close-up render. The ear part draws all three on its own centreline, 8.65, and their sizes are estimated; its contract says so.

thickness.note: datasheet - FS's product page for #72911: "rugged 1.5mm cold-rolled steel".

top.note: drawing - the plan view. Rings centred 35.7, 131.1, 241.5, 351.9 and 447.3 mm along the 483, so 95.4 between the outer pairs and 110.4 between the inner, symmetric about the middle. The front view of the same drawing puts the five posts at the same five places; it is a second view of one model and not a second source.

top-arms.note: drawing - each arm sweeps up from the flat tray into the upright ear, and the ring-profile view draws that as a sloped web. Built as a flat strip of floor, an upright ear, and a web on the arm's outer edge: one plate whose top edge follows the slope. The arm's floor stops 15.4 mm short of the rail face, as drawn.

top-rings.note: drawing - each ring is an open loop: the slit at its top front corner, 2.2 mm, is where a cable is pressed in. It also turns through 360 degrees and lifts out, and is drawn fitted, across the tray. FS's mark, stamped on the tray by the right-hand ring, is not drawn: a vendor mark never is.

views.note: drawing - left and right are the ring-profile view of the same drawing. The bottom is the plan again from underneath - the strip, the arms and the slots - without the fillets where the arms meet the strip, and without the five round bosses of the rings' seats that the drawing and FS's render of the underside both show. NO REFERENCE IMAGE EXISTS FOR THE REAR: it is the front view's elevation turned round.
